title: Verify invalid tank-volume curves across file loading and API updates
research_next_step: Verify whether the separately observed metric EN_VOLCURVE nominal-diameter discrepancy changes file round-trips or simulated results, using the unchanged library and valid synthetic networks in fixed units. Distinguish presentation-only differences from consequential behavior before proposing separate work. Prepare the existing #883 evidence/scope inquiry under current contribution and compute review rules; no implementation before maintainer confirmation.
problem: The real pinned library accepts decreasing and interior-dip water-storage volume curves through file loading, API assignment and later curve edits. Direct decreasing assignment returns a NaN diameter without an API error; increasing requested depth yields decreasing initial volume. No process crash or operational consequence is established.
humanitarian_relevance: Clear validation may improve reliability of water-network analysis tools. No measured effect on drinking-water safety, utility decisions or resource use.

evidence.claim: Reporter says invalid tank-volume curves can produce decreasing volume while filling and a floating-point exception when negative area is converted to diameter. These runtime claims have not been independently reproduced.

Pinned file initialization and two API assignment routes derive area from endpoint slope. Curve point/bulk setters check increasing X but not Y; generic decreasing pump curves must remain valid. Existing curve/node tests inspected, not run.

Thirty-four native-library cases pass as current-behavior assertions across GPM/LPS units, three curve shapes and five entry paths, plus cylindrical and decreasing-pump controls. All open/assignment/hydraulic-initialization calls succeed. Direct decreasing assignment yields NaN diameter; interior dips and subsequent edits retain finite diameter while volume decreases with greater requested depth. Metric EN_VOLCURVE assignment also yields 0.3048 times the diameter from file/EN_settankdata routes for the same valid curve. All 144 tracked source files remain byte-identical before build and after probes.

The unchanged native CMake baseline passes: 88 Boost cases across six binaries, plus two threaded runs returning status zero. All six CTest entries pass and the unregistered string-helper binary passes separately. All 34 behavior cases pass again against the test-enabled library; 144 tracked files remain byte-identical. Bounded searches found historical unit-changing/parameter issues, but not a matching report of the fixed-unit EN_VOLCURVE nominal-diameter discrepancy.
